extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and national / international patent Office staff (receiving Offices, International Searching Authorities, International Preliminary Examining Authorities, designated Offices)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements governing formalities for PCT international applications: required disclosures (including biological deposits and sequence listings), fees and payment time limits, priority document obligations, competence of receiving Offices, determination of international filing date, and procedures for missing or erroneous parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to deposited biological material — required indications
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to deposited biological material must indicate the name and the address of the depositary institution; the date of deposit of the biological material with that institution; the accession number given to the deposit by that institution; and any additional matter of which the International Bureau has been notified pursuant to Rule 13 bis.7(a)(i), provided that the requirement to indicate that matter was published in the Gazette in accordance with Rule 13 bis.7(c) at least two months before the filing of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include a reference to deposited biological material or failure to include an indication in accordance with paragraph (a) shall have no consequence in any designated State whose national law does not require such reference or such indication in a national application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for furnishing indications for deposited biological material (Rule 13 bis.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the indications required for a reference to deposited biological material is not included in the international application as filed but is furnished to the International Bureau, different timing rules apply: (i) within 16 months from the priority date the indication is considered furnished in time; (ii) after 16 months it is considered furnished on the last day of that time limit if it reaches the International Bureau before technical preparations for international publication are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A designated Office may require earlier furnishing than 16 months if its national law so requires in respect of national applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples of deposited biological material (Rule 13 bis.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: No furnishing of samples of deposited biological material referred to in an international application shall take place, except with applicant authorization, before expiration of applicable time limits after which national processing may start under Articles 23 and 40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if the applicant performs the acts referred to in Articles 22 or 39 after international publication but before expiration of the said time limits, furnishing may take place once those acts have been performed. Notwithstanding the previous provision, furnishing may take place under the national law of a designated Office as soon as international publication has the effects of compulsory national publication of an unexamined national application.

rubrics_metrics.name: National requirements: notification and publication regarding biological deposits (Rule 13 bis.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any national Office may notify the International Bureau of national-law requirements about matters to be included in references to deposited biological material, or earlier times for furnishing indications; each national Office shall notify depositary institutions permitted under its law; the International Bureau shall promptly publish such notifications in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications may include additional matters required in national applications or requirements that certain indications be furnished earlier than 16 months from the priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing procedure before the International Searching Authority (Rule 13 ter.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application contains nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences that must be included in a sequence listing, the International Searching Authority may invite the applicant to furnish a sequence listing complying with the standard in the Administrative Instructions, and to pay a late furnishing fee where applicable, within a time limit fixed in the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to furnish the required listing and pay the fee within the time limit, the ISA is only required to search to the extent a meaningful search can be carried out without the listing. Any sequence listing not contained in the application as filed shall not form part of the international application, though the applicant may amend the description in relation to a sequence listing pursuant to Article 34(2)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late furnishing fee for sequence listings (Rule 13 ter.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Searching Authority may require payment of a late furnishing fee for a sequence listing furnished in response to an invitation; the amount is determined by the ISA but shall not exceed 25% of the international filing fee referred to in item 1 of the Schedule of Fees (excluding any sheet fees for >30 sheets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not furnished, the ISA's search obligation is limited to what is meaningful without the sequence listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure before the International Preliminary Examining Authority (Rule 13 ter.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 13 ter.1 applies mutatis mutandis to the procedure before the International Preliminary Examining Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirement for designated Offices (Rule 13 ter.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall require an applicant to furnish a sequence listing other than one complying with the standard provided for in the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal fee (Rule 14.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any receiving Office may require the applicant to pay a transmittal fee for receiving the international application, transmitting copies to the International Bureau and the competent ISA, and performing other tasks as receiving Office; the fee is for the receiving Office's own benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount, if any, is fixed by the receiving Office and must be paid within one month from the date of receipt of the international application; the amount payable is that applicable on the date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: International filing fee — obligation and amount (Rule 15.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each international application is subject to payment of an international filing fee for the benefit of the International Bureau; the amount is as set out in the Schedule of Fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee is payable in the currency or one of the currencies prescribed by the receiving Office (prescribed currency). Rules govern transfer and conversion into Swiss francs or other currencies for transmission to the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for payment of international filing fee (Rule 15.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international filing fee shall be paid to the receiving Office within one month from the date of receipt of the international application; the amount payable is the amount applicable on that date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of international filing fee (Rule 15.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall refund the international filing fee to the applicant if (i) the determination under Article 11(1) is negative, (ii) if before transmittal of the record copy to the International Bureau the international application is withdrawn or considered withdrawn, or (iii) if, due to prescriptions concerning national security, the international application is not treated as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee — right to require and payment (Rule 16.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each International Searching Authority may require payment of a search fee for carrying out the international search and related tasks; the search fee is collected by the receiving Office and payable in the prescribed currency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prescribed currency differs from the ISA's fixed currency, conversion and transfer rules apply; time limit and amount payable follow the provisions of Rule 15.3 mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of search fee (Rule 16.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall refund the search fee to the applicant if (i) the determination under Article 11(1) is negative, (ii) if before transmittal of the search copy to the ISA the application is withdrawn or considered withdrawn, or (iii) if, due to national security prescriptions, the application is not treated as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial refund of search fee when earlier search taken into account (Rule 16.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ISA takes into account the results of an earlier search in carrying out the international search under Rule 41.1, that Authority shall refund the search fee paid to the extent and under conditions provided in the agreement under Article 16(3)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time limits for payment — invitation by receiving Office (Rule 16 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If by the time fees are due the receiving Office finds no fees were paid or the amount is insufficient to cover required fees, it shall invite the applicant to pay the required amount (including where applicable the late payment fee) within one month from the date of the invitation; payments received before the invitation are considered received before expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant fails to pay within the invitation time limit, the receiving Office shall, subject to paragraph (e), make the applicable declaration under Article 14(3) and proceed under Rule 29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late payment fee (Rule 16 bis.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of fees in response to an invitation may be subjected by the receiving Office to a late payment fee, which shall be either (i) 50% of the amount of unpaid fees specified in the invitation, or (ii) if the amount calculated under (i) is less than the transmittal fee, an amount equal to the transmittal fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The late payment fee shall not exceed 50% of the international filing fee (item 1 of Schedule of Fees), not taking into account any fee for each sheet in excess of 30 sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to submit priority document (Rule 17.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority of an earlier national or international application is claimed under Article 8, a certified copy of that earlier application (priority document) shall, unless already filed with the receiving Office, be submitted by the applicant to the International Bureau or to the receiving Office not later than 16 months after the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any copy received after that time limit shall be considered received on the last day of that time limit if it reaches the IB before the date of international publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for receiving Office to prepare/transmit priority document (Rule 17.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the priority document is issued by the receiving Office, the applicant may request the receiving Office to prepare and transmit the priority document to the International Bureau instead of submitting it; such request must be made not later than 16 months after the priority date and may be subject to a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining priority document from a digital library (Rule 17.1(b-bis))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the priority document is made available to the International Bureau from a digital library prior to international publication, the applicant may request the International Bureau, prior to international publication, to obtain the priority document from such digital library instead of submitting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and opportunity to furnish priority document (Rule 17.1(c)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If none of the procedures for supplying the priority document are complied with, any designated Office may, subject to paragraph (d), disregard the priority claim, but no designated Office shall disregard it before giving the applicant an opportunity to furnish the priority document within a reasonable time; exceptions exist where the earlier application was filed with that Office or the priority document is available from a digital library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of copies of the priority document (Rule 17.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant complies with Rule 17.1, the International Bureau shall, at the specific request of a designated Office, promptly but not prior to international publication furnish a copy of the priority document to that Office; no such Office shall ask the applicant to furnish it; translations are not required before the expiration of the applicable time limit under Article 22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IB shall not make copies public prior to international publication. After publication, IB shall furnish a copy to any person upon request and subject to reimbursement of cost unless the international application was withdrawn or the priority claim was withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence and nationality of applicant (Rule 18.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an applicant is a resident or national of a Contracting State depends on that State's national law and is decided by the receiving Office; possession of a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in a State shall be considered residence; a legal entity constituted according to national law shall be considered a national of that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the application is filed with the International Bureau as receiving Office, the IB shall request the relevant national Office to decide the question in specific Administrative Instructions circumstances and inform the applicant, who has an opportunity to submit arguments directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applicants — entitlement to file (Rule 18.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are two or more applicants, the right to file an international application exists if at least one of them is entitled to file an international application according to Article 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on national law qualifications to file (Rule 18.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall, from time to time, publish information on various national laws regarding who is qualified (inventor, successor in title, owner, or other) to file a national application and shall warn that the effect of the international application in any designated State may depend on whether the person designated as applicant is qualified under that State's law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file — competent receiving Office (Rule 19.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, the international application shall be filed, at the applicant's option, with the national Office of residence, the national Office of nationality, or with the International Bureau. Contracting States may agree that another national Office or intergovernmental organization shall act as receiving Office for residents/nationals of the former State, and the Assembly may appoint receiving Offices for certain purposes under Article 9(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding delegation agreements, the national Office of the delegating State remains the competent receiving Office for purposes of Article 15(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applicants — satisfying receiving Office requirements (Rule 19.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are two or more applicants, the requirements of Rule 19.1 are met if the receiving Office with which the international application is filed is the national Office of or acting for a Contracting State of which at least one applicant is a resident or national; the application may be filed with the International Bureau if at least one applicant is resident or national of a Contracting State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of delegation of receiving Office duties (Rule 19.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agreement delegating receiving Office duties under Rule 19.1(b) shall be promptly notified to the International Bureau by the State which delegates those duties, and the International Bureau shall promptly publish the notification in the Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal to the International Bureau as receiving Office (Rule 19.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an international application is filed with a national Office acting as receiving Office but that national Office is not competent, or the application is not in a language accepted by that national Office but is accepted by the IB as receiving Office, or other specified circumstances, the national Office may be considered to have received the application on behalf of the IB; it shall promptly transmit it to the IB (unless national security prevents transmission), and the transmittal may be subject to a fee equal to the national Office's transmittal fee. The application transmitted is considered received by the IB on the date received by the national Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the purposes of Rules 14.1(c), 15.3 and 16.1(f), where the application was transmitted to the IB under this Rule, the date of receipt for fee purposes shall be considered the date the application was actually received by the IB; paragraph (c) clarifies that the last sentence of paragraph (b) does not apply to that provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of compliance with Article 11(1) and international filing date (Rule 20.1–20.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptly after receipt, the receiving Office shall determine whether the papers fulfill Article 11(1). If positive, the receiving Office shall accord the international filing date as the date of receipt, stamp the request as prescribed, make that copy the record copy, notify the applicant of the international application number and filing date, and send a copy of the notification to the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Article 11(1)(iii)(c) it is sufficient to indicate the applicant's name in a way that allows identity to be established even if misspelled or abbreviated. For Article 11(1)(ii) it is sufficient that the parts appearing to be description and claims be in a language accepted by the receiving Office under Rule 12.1(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects under Article 11(1) — invitation to correct or confirm incorporation by reference (Rule 20.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office finds any Article 11(1) requirements are not or appear not to be fulfilled, it shall promptly invite the applicant to either furnish the required correction under Article 11(2) or (where elements relate to Article 11(1)(iii)(d) or (e)) to confirm that the element is incorporated by reference under Rule 4.18, and to make observations within the applicable time limit under Rule 20.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant furnishes the required correction within the time limit, the receiving Office shall accord the later date as the international filing date. If the receiving Office later discovers it erred in issuing an invitation, it shall act as if Article 11(1) requirements were fulfilled on receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative determination under Article 11(1) (Rule 20.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no correction or confirmation is received within the applicable time limit, or the application still does not fulfill Article 11(1), the receiving Office shall promptly notify the applicant that the application is not and will not be treated as an international application and indicate reasons, notify the IB that the number will not be used, keep the papers and related correspondence as provided in Rule 93.1, and send a copy to the IB where requested under Article 25(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing parts — completion, incorporation by reference, and filing date effects (Rule 20.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a part of the description, claims or drawings is missing (but not an entire element of Article 11(1)(iii)(d) or (e)), the receiving Office shall invite the applicant to either furnish the missing part or confirm incorporation by reference, and to make observations within the time limit. If the missing part is furnished on or before the date on which all Article 11(1) requirements are fulfilled and within the applicable time limit, it shall be included and the receiving Office shall accord as international filing date the date on which all requirements are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If furnished after the date on which the requirements were fulfilled but within the time limit, the receiving Office shall include the part and correct the international filing date to the date it received that part and notify the applicant. The applicant may, within one month of notification of correction, request that the missing part be disregarded (i.e., treated as not furnished) and the correction not made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erroneously filed elements and parts — correction and filing date effects (Rule 20.5 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an entire element of Article 11(1)(iii)(d) or (e) or a part of description/claims/drawings is or appears to be erroneously filed (including all drawings erroneously filed), the receiving Office shall invite the applicant to either furnish the correct element/part or confirm incorporation by reference, and to make observations within the time limit. If the correct element/part is furnished before all Article 11(1) requirements are fulfilled but within the time limit, the correct element/part is included, the erroneously filed element/part removed, and the receiving Office shall accord as the international filing date the date on which all requirements are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the correct element/part is furnished after the date on which requirements were fulfilled but within the time limit, the receiving Office shall include the correct element/part, remove the erroneously filed one, correct the international filing date to the date on which it received the correct element/part and notify the applicant. If a correct element/part is considered to have been contained in the application on the earlier date under Rule 20.6(b), the erroneously filed element/part remains and the filing date is the date on which Article 11(1) requirements were fulfilled.
